title: When one object pushes another, it is pushed back equally
summary: Whenever one object exerts a force on a second, it feels an equal force back in the opposite direction.
body: OpenStax Physics states Newton's third law this way: whenever a first object exerts a force on a second, the first experiences a force equal in size and opposite in direction. Forces occur in pairs, on two different objects. The page's everyday picture is stubbing a toe: the toe hits the surface, and the surface hits the toe back. Throwing a ball is offered as another pair. Urone and Hinrichs, 26 March 2020. The law is about the pair of forces, not about the two objects having the same mass.
